language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, my name is Brandon.
Today is my birthday. My father is going to celebrate it with me in this pizza restaurant. We got a table by the window, so we can watch the beautiful sunset.

My birthday is in winter, so the sunset will start around 5 PM. But my father’s birthday is in summer. During the summer, the sunset starts around 7 PM. So in winter, the day time is shorter and night time is longer than in summer. Weird huh?
Look, the sun is going down while the sky is turning black. Isn’t it wonderful to watch how the day fades into night?

Brandon, the reason that we have to watch the sunset at different times in summer and winter, is because of the Earth’s two motions: rotation and revolution. These two motions cause the day and night, and the four seasons.

outro.text: The moving of one object around a bigger object is called revolution. So, the earth is revolving around the sun. It takes the earth 365 days to complete one journey across the sun; exactly one year! Coincidence?

The spinning of the earth causes day and night. What does the revolution of the earth around the sun cause? It's the seasons! Let's see how that works.

outro.text: Now I know that the Earth’s revolution causes the four seasons. When the northern hemisphere is tilted towards the sun, it receives longer hours of sunlight and shorter night time. That means the northern hemisphere is in its days of summer. At the same time, the southern hemisphere is in the winter. This is why it’s summer in Australia when it is winter in the United States.
